setlist.title: Beat It On Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Smokestack Lightning** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls Smokestack Lightning a scorching highlight of the show; Pigpen stretches out on the classic, possibly at his best ever, including an 'I've been gone so long' passage [5][6][7]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Jerry's guitar tone on the first Truckin' lead is praised, likened to B.B. King [8]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw is described as slightly off, though the band is otherwise tight [5]
- **Run Rudolph Run** (1 other source): Noted as the first time the band played Run Rudolph Run [2]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Mexicali Blues turns up sandwiched between two parts of The Other One [13]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 other source): Johnny B Goode is listed as the encore [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mister Charlie**: rare: 13 archived performances [17]
- **Run Rudolph Run**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 7 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd71-12-04.sbd.lai.6256.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 132 min; rated 4.38/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: This tape lacks Johnny B. Goode, and Cumberland fades in partway; Bass drum has a funky thump picked up by the mic; piano shows distortion peaks; Distortion or vibration from Billy's bass drum pedal is audible on the recording [1][6][14]
- **gd1971-12-04.sbd.fixed.miller.110186.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 137 min; rated 3.25/5 by 12 [2]
- **gd1971-12-04.sbd.miller.110128.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 130 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1971-12-04.120948.d190e.weinberg-moore-berger.flac16**: audience recording; 14 songs; 85 min [4]

## Around the show

- Keith is fully integrated into the band, and Pigpen is back strongly after a long absence from illness [8]
- Pigpen is healthy at this winter 1971 show [10]
- Reviewer's first Dead show at age 16; friends rode the subway from Brooklyn to Manhattan [14]
- Felt Forum crowd was full of New Yorkers, with heavy pot smoke and drug use [14]
- Reviewer thinks Donna can be heard at the end of One More Saturday Night, perhaps her first show [15]
- The blues and rock and roll setlist differs somewhat from what the band normally played that year [5]
- Shows from this period share a uniform sound and presentation, so none stands out over the others [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-12-04.sbd.lai.6256.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard transferred through MR, DAT, another C and DAT, then CDR; circulated via Mike Lai, with thanks to Paul Bottiglio [1]
- **gd1971-12-04.sbd.fixed.miller.110186.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat [2]. Also: Fixed soundboard version by Miller, offered as an upgrade to an earlier copy, shnid 110128; This soundboard is a fixed version prepared by Charlie Miller [2][16]
- **gd1971-12-04.sbd.miller.110128.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat [3]
- **gd1971-12-04.120948.d190e.weinberg-moore-berger.flac16**: taped by Jerry Moore and Marty Weinberg; transferred by Rob Berger; source: flac16: aud reel master>reel>dat, taped by Marty Weinberg, Jerry Moore's copy transferred by Rob Berger [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by rocktourdatabase.com: [Grateful Dead | rocktourdatabase.com](https://rocktourdatabase.com/content/grateful-dead-32) [18]
